description: A four by four grid of knobs with a position that walks in x and y, after Make Noise's René

params.text: Moves the position to that cell for as long as it is held down, and lights while it is held
Sets the voltage that cell sends, -2V at fully counter-clockwise to 2V fully clockwise

inputs.text: Moves the position up one row on each rising edge above 1V, wrapping from the top row round to the bottom
Moves the position down one row on each rising edge above 1V, wrapping from the bottom row round to the top
Moves the position one column left on each rising edge above 1V, wrapping from the first column round to the last
Moves the position one column right on each rising edge above 1V, wrapping from the last column round to the first
Adds its voltage, rounded and held between 0 and 3, to the column on every sample rather than once, so anything above half a volt sends the position racing along the row
Adds its voltage, rounded and held between 0 and 3, to the row on every sample rather than once, so anything above half a volt sends the position racing down the column
Moves the position to the first cell of the first row on each rising edge above 1V, and cancels any step arriving in the same sample
Moves the position to the first column on each rising edge above 1V, leaving the row where it is, and cancels any step arriving in the same sample
Moves the position to the first row on each rising edge above 1V, leaving the column where it is, and cancels any step arriving in the same sample

outputs.text: The voltage of the knob at the current position, exactly as that knob is set
The voltage of the knob at the current position, rounded to the nearest semitone
The knob in its own column, on whichever row the position is on
The knob in its own row, in whichever column the position is on

notes: nothing moves until a clock is patched to one of the four step inputs; with none patched the position stays on the first cell and every output holds that cell's value
the position wraps in both directions and there is no length setting, so the walk always covers all four columns and all four rows
the knob settings are saved with the patch; the position is not, and starts again at the first cell every time the patch is opened
